name: Brad Parscale

summary.text: Brad Parscale is a San Antonio digital marketer whose firm Giles-Parscale built Donald Trump's exploratory campaign website in 2015 for $1,500 and became the 2016 campaign's largest vendor. He was named the campaign's digital media director in June 2016, was interviewed by the House Intelligence Committee in October 2017, and later served as Trump's 2020 campaign manager. He has said the campaign relied on RNC voter data rather than Cambridge Analytica's raw data.

facts.claim: In early 2015 Parscale's firm Giles-Parscale was hired to create a website for Trump's exploratory campaign for $1,500; in June 2016 Parscale was named digital media director of the Trump campaign, overseeing digital media, online fundraising and some traditional media strategy.

sources.title: Trump's digital campaign director was paid $1,500 to set up his election website. Then he raked in $94 million when Trump won
Inside Trump's $100 million man's rapid rise to power

facts.claim: CNBC reported, citing FEC filings, that Giles-Parscale was paid about $94 million by the Trump campaign, the RNC and the Trump Make America Great Again committee in the 2016 cycle, with the campaign paying nearly $88 million; Parscale said the vast majority passed through his firm to buy advertising.
facts.quote: the campaign shelled out the majority of the money, nearly $88 million

sources.title: Trump's digital campaign director was paid $1,500 to set up his election website. Then he raked in $94 million when Trump won
Inside Trump's $100 million man's rapid rise to power

facts.claim: Parscale has said the Trump campaign never used Cambridge Analytica's raw data and that he brought the firm in because Matt Oczkowski, a digital expert he wanted to hire, was under contract there; CNN reported that Parscale and Jared Kushner decided in late September or early October 2016 to use only RNC data for the general election after tests showed it was more accurate.
facts.quote: the decision to use only RNC data for the general election came in late September or early October from Jared Kushner and Parscale

sources.title: Trump campaign phased out use of Cambridge Analytica data before election
Trump campaign and Cambridge Analytica

facts.claim: Parscale was interviewed by the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in a closed executive session on October 24, 2017; the transcript was later released. Before the interview he said he had no first-hand knowledge of foreign interference and that the only collaboration he knew of was with staff provided to the campaign by Facebook, Google and Twitter.

facts.claim: The Associated Press reported in June 2018 that Parscale was a part owner of Cloud Commerce, the publicly traded parent of Data Propria, a firm led by former Cambridge Analytica head of product Matt Oczkowski; Cloud Commerce had bought Parscale's digital marketing business in August 2017. Parscale told the AP he had not yet begun awarding contracts for the 2020 campaign.
facts.quote: Parscale is a part owner of Cloud Commerce, Data Propria's publicly traded parent company

facts.claim: In July 2020 the Campaign Legal Center filed an FEC complaint alleging the Trump campaign masked nearly $170 million of spending through firms headed by Parscale, including American Made Media Consultants, which it said had been paid over $106 million; the campaign denied wrongdoing, saying it reported all payments to AMMC as required. This is an allegation.
facts.quote: The campaign reports all payments to AMMC as required by the FEC.
